projectName: Web Block Clock and Bitcoin Node Presence
description: Connect the web dashboard to the household Bitcoin node stack with an optional block clock and compact chain-status panel powered by local Bitcoin RPC, reinforcing the sovereign operating posture without turning the app into a full node console.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after Feature-20 stabilizes the web shell and dashboard layout enough to absorb one additional dashboard card without churn.

principles: Timechain Presence - the dashboard should feel connected to Bitcoin itself, not only to the accounting database
Optional, Not Fragile - local node integration must never prevent the rest of the web app from loading
Compact Operator Signal - expose the node metrics that inform confidence and action, not a full console clone
Local-First Sovereignty - query only household-controlled infrastructure such as local bitcoind and local Electrum-compatible services
Phone First, Desktop Better - the block clock card must read clearly on mobile while allowing richer density on desktop

techStack.backendFramework: FastAPI web service with request-safe service adapters
techStack.frontend: Existing responsive web shell with dashboard cards and lightweight polling
techStack.testing: pytest API tests + frontend smoke coverage
techStack.coreDependencies: bitcoind JSON-RPC + existing web dashboard service layer

userStories.title: Optional Bitcoin node config and runtime service seam
acceptanceCriteria: Add optional web configuration for local Bitcoin RPC access using cookie auth or explicit credentials
Validate chain-status config without making web startup fail when the feature is disabled
Create a small service adapter responsible for querying blockchain, network, and mempool status from bitcoind
Keep the integration isolated from core accounting query classes
userStories.testStrategy: pytest config and service tests covering enabled, disabled, and unreachable-node cases
userStories.closureNotes: Added optional Bitcoin RPC config and request-safe chain status service seam without making the rest of the web app depend on node availability.

userStories.title: Chain status API and canonical read model
acceptanceCriteria: Expose chain-status data through a stable web payload with explicit nullability for unavailable metrics
Include current block height, header height, sync posture, last block age, peer count, and mempool summary
Represent degraded or unreachable node states as operator-readable warnings rather than raw exceptions
Keep the payload compact enough for dashboard polling
userStories.testStrategy: pytest API tests for available, syncing, unavailable, and disabled states
userStories.closureNotes: Shipped canonical chain-status payloads and API coverage for available, syncing, unavailable, and disabled states.

userStories.title: Dashboard block clock card
acceptanceCriteria: Render a compact dashboard card showing height, time since last block, sync status, peers, and mempool activity
Fit the card cleanly into the existing mobile-first dashboard layout without overwhelming portfolio information
Provide a clear unavailable or stale presentation when node data is missing or old
Use terminology suitable for operators familiar with Bitcoin but not dependent on terminal-style dense output
userStories.testStrategy: frontend smoke coverage plus targeted rendering tests for normal and degraded states
userStories.closureNotes: Integrated the Bitcoin Timechain card into the dashboard with compact operator-facing metrics and degraded-state rendering.

userStories.title: Refresh policy, stale-state logic, and UX polish
acceptanceCriteria: Define a conservative refresh cadence appropriate for single-operator dashboard use
Show freshness information such as last update time or stale indicator where appropriate
Avoid aggressive polling when the node is unreachable or disabled
Preserve fast dashboard interaction even when chain-status calls are slower than portfolio reads
userStories.testStrategy: manual behavior verification plus targeted stale-state tests
userStories.closureNotes: Implemented freshness/stale indicators and conservative refresh behavior so slower node calls do not dominate dashboard interaction.

userStories.title: Operator docs and deployment notes
acceptanceCriteria: Document required environment variables and cookie-auth setup for local bitcoind access
Explain degraded behavior when chain status is disabled or unavailable
Record the intended scope boundary so future work can add verification or broadcast features without reinterpreting Feature-22
Update planning metadata and progress notes once implementation lands
userStories.testStrategy: manual doc review + deployment checklist validation
userStories.closureNotes: Documented local bitcoind environment variables and scope boundaries, and aligned planning metadata with the shipped feature.

high: If node integration can break or materially slow the dashboard, trust in the web app will drop quickly
If the card tries to do too much, it will dilute the portfolio dashboard rather than strengthen it
medium: RPC availability and auth configuration may vary across self-hosted deployments
Stale node data could be misread as live without explicit degraded-state language
low: The feature is read-only and can be isolated behind a narrow service seam
bitcoind already exposes the core status metrics needed for a useful first pass

preFlightChecklist: Confirm exact metric set for v1 block clock card
Choose whether chain status lives inside /api/portfolio/dashboard or under its own route
Choose refresh cadence and stale threshold
Confirm cookie-file path handling for production deployment on numenor
